title: Retention & Revalidation Policy for Redwood-Verified Performance Profiles
creator: Ava Chen
description: As Redwood’s catalog of verified performance profiles grows, we need a clear lifecycle policy that balances signal freshness, operational cost, and compatibility with model pinning. This ticket defines retention windows, automated revalidation cadence, archival behavior, and the UX/notification flow for profile staleness and republishing. The goal is to ensure customers relying on Redwood-verified latency/throughput/cost numbers have up-to-date guidance while limiting unnecessary rebenching costs.
acceptance_criteria: Define retention windows and staleness thresholds for verified profiles (active, warning, archived)
Implement automated revalidation job that runs lightweight smoke benchmarks against profile samples on a configurable cadence
Console shows profile age, staleness state, last-validated timestamp, and a suggested action (revalidate, archive, mark-for-review)
Notification pipeline that alerts model owners and affected customers when a profile goes from active -> warning or when revalidation fails
Migration guidance for pinned model versions: if a profile is archived or significantly regresses, provide automatic pin-migration suggestions and a rollback path
Measure revalidation cost delta and ensure revalidation budget is tracked in Optimize dashboard
notes_or_decisions: Retention policy proposal: active=90 days since last full validation, warning=90-180 days (show 'stale' badge), archived>180 days (hidden from primary catalog)
Revalidation cadence: lightweight daily sampling for high-traffic models, 30-day full revalidation for catalog models, configurable per-project in Dedicated/Private
Regression thresholds: latency >5% or cost per token >10% relative to published profile triggers manual review; throughput drop >10% triggers immediate investigation
Revalidation implementation will reuse ENG's verified-benchmark-pipeline (PM-6342) and add a smaller smoke harness for cadence runs
Profiles remain immutable once published; republish creates a new profile version and the console links old -> new. Auto-migration suggested but requires owner approval for pinned models

implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define thresholds and add profile metadata fields (ENG). Phase 2: Build smoke revalidation job and pipeline integration with verified-benchmarks. Phase 3: Console UI changes + notification integration. Phase 4: Gradual rollout, monitor revalidation cost and customer feedback.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: repeated revalidations increase infra costs. Mitigation: tiered cadence (sample vs full) and cost cap per project. Risk: false positives from noisy samples. Mitigation: require regression to be observed in two consecutive runs before triggering owner notification.
test_plan: Unit tests for metadata migration, end-to-end revalidation run in staging that compares baseline profile values, canary release for console UI to 10% of catalog owners, smoke tests to verify notification delivery.
estimated_cost_notes: Initial weekly smoke runs estimated at ~12 GPU-hours/week for current catalog; full revalidation of 120 models estimated ~180 GPU-hours/month. Optimize to propose batching/quantization to reduce costs.
